stories.title: Slate, OneIM Acquire Eight Grocery-Anchored Centers in Greater Oslo
stories.excerpt: Slate Asset Management and One Investment Management have agreed to acquire a portfolio of eight grocery-anchored retail parks in Norway from Tellus Eiendom AS for approximately €250 million (US$279 million). The portfolio is located in the Greater Oslo region and is anchored by Norway’s leading grocery operators and discount retailers. “We are pleased to be expanding our European Essential real estate platform with this significant acquisition,” said Brady Welch, co-founding partner of Toronto-based Slate Asset Management. “These eight retail parks sit in dominant locations along major transport corridors around Oslo. The portfolio is anchored by Norway’s strongest grocery operators and benefits from CPI-linked lease structures, designed to provide durable, inflation-protected cash flows. We look forward to applying our active management to unlock the portfolio’s full potential through value-add enhancements.” The portfolio is dominated by essential tenants serving non-discretionary, everyday needs, including Coop, NorgesGruppen and Reitan Retail, three of Norway’s largest and most established grocery operators. The acquisition builds on Slate and OneIM’s existing partnership and follows their investments in a portfolio of five grocery-anchored retail properties in Greater Copenhagen, as well as a portfolio of four essential real estate properties in Germany. Slate Asset Management has been advised by Schjødt, ABG Sundal Collier, Crowe and Veridian. The post Slate, OneIM Acquire Eight Grocery-Anchored Centers in Greater Oslo appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Slate & OneIM acquire 8 grocery-anchored retail parks near Oslo for €250M (~$279M).
Portfolio anchored by Norway's top 3 grocers; CPI-linked leases protect against inflation.
Expands Slate/OneIM essential retail platform across Europe (Copenhagen, Germany already held).
stories.summary: Slate Asset Management and One Investment Management acquired a portfolio of eight grocery-anchored retail parks in Greater Oslo from Tellus Eiendom AS for approximately €250 million (~$279 million). The properties are dominated by Norway's largest grocery operators—Coop, NorgesGruppen, and Reitan Retail—and feature CPI-linked lease structures designed to provide inflation-protected cash flows. This acquisition builds on the partners' existing European platform, which already includes five grocery-anchored properties in Copenhagen and four essential-use properties in Germany.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Slate and OneIM's focus on essential retail in Northern Europe signals capital redeployment away from office/discretionary retail toward inflation-hedged grocery anchors. However, this does not materially affect U.S. multifamily supply, demand, or financing dynamics where TCR operates.

stories.title: Northmarq Secures $50M Refinancing of Multifamily Asset in MN
stories.excerpt: Northmarq has arranged $50 million in financing for Ardor on the Bluffs, a 235-unit mid-rise multifamily community in Bloomington, Minnesota. Located at 3701 American Blvd, the complex is located just minutes from MSP International Airport and the Mall of America. Northmarq’s Minneapolis Debt + Equity team, led by Dan Trebil, arranged the financing on behalf of the borrower through a relationship with a life insurance company. “Ownership and management have done a tremendous job at Ardor, and this new financing will allow ownership flexibility as they complete their lease-up,” said Trebil. Completed in December 2024, Ardor on the Bluffs is a six-story luxury multifamily community offering studio, one- and two-bedroom apartment homes. Situated in Bloomington’s South Loop district, Ardor on the Bluffs provides convenient access to a wide range of employment centers and transportation corridors. The surrounding area also offers a selection of shopping, dining and entertainment destinations The post Northmarq Secures $50M Refinancing of Multifamily Asset in MN appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranges $50M refi for Ardor on the Bluffs, 235-unit luxury mid-rise in Bloomington, MN.
Property completed Dec 2024; financing via life insurance company supports lease-up completion.
Located near MSP Airport and Mall of America; positioned in high-access employment/retail corridor.
stories.summary: Northmarq's Minneapolis Debt + Equity team arranged $50 million in financing for Ardor on the Bluffs, a 235-unit luxury mid-rise multifamily community completed in December 2024 in Bloomington, Minnesota. The six-story asset, located at 3701 American Blvd near MSP International Airport and the Mall of America, received the refinancing through a relationship with a life insurance company to provide ownership flexibility during lease-up. The property is situated in Bloomington's South Loop district with convenient access to employment centers and transportation corridors.
stories.impact: Signals life insurance capital active in financing newly completed multifamily assets in MSP submarket. The refi timing (mid-Dec 2024 completion into Q1 2025 refi) suggests strong lender confidence in South Loop Bloomington absorption fundamentals, particularly near airport/retail nodes. Indicates stable debt markets and lender appetite for Class-A product in secondary metros.

stories.title: Gary Barnett, Lisa Silverstein Among Honorees at Upcoming 131st REBNY Annual
stories.excerpt: The Real Estate Board of New York has announced the honorees for the 131st REBNY Annual, celebrating the people whose work and leadership have helped shape the city. The celebration will take place on Thursday, Jan. 14, 2027 at the Waldorf Astoria New York. This year’s honorees will include the following: The John E. Zuccotti Public Service Award: Jessica Tisch, New York City Police Commissioner The Bernard H. Mendik Lifetime Leadership in Real Estate Award: Gary Barnett, Founder and Chairman, Extell Development Company The Harry B. Helmsley Distinguished New Yorker Award: David Arena, Head of Global Corporate Real Estate, JPMorgan Chase The Kenneth R. Gerrety Humanitarian Award: Lisa Silverstein, CEO, Silverstein Properties The Louis Smadbeck Memorial Broker Recognition Award: James Nelson, Principal and Head of U.S. Investment Sales, Avison Young The George M. Brooker Management Executive of the Year Award: Marisa Gadlin, Chief Administrative Officer and Head of Core Holdings, Rockefeller Group. The Young Real Estate Professional of the Year Award: Caroline Merck, Senior Vice President, CBRE “This year’s honorees have each made an extraordinary contribution to New York City,” said REBNY President James Whelan.“Their leadership, service and commitment to New York reflect what the REBNY Annual has celebrated for more than a century, and we look forward to recognizing their achievements.” The post Gary Barnett, Lisa Silverstein Among Honorees at Upcoming 131st REBNY Annual appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: REBNY honors Gary Barnett (Extell), Lisa Silverstein (Silverstein Properties), and 4 others Jan. 14, 2027.
Recognizes lifetime leadership in NYC real estate development and corporate real estate.
Ceremony at Waldorf Astoria; 131st annual celebration of industry figures.
stories.summary: The Real Estate Board of New York announced honorees for its 131st Annual celebration on January 14, 2027 at the Waldorf Astoria. Gary Barnett, Founder and Chairman of Extell Development Company, received the Bernard H. stories.title: Ambrose Breaks Ground on Two Facilities at Indianapolis Logistics Park
stories.excerpt: Ambrose has broken ground on two buildings at the Indianapolis Logistics Park – Northwest, a 104-acre modern industrial park in Whitestown, Indiana, part of Greater Indianapolis. The two buildings are being developed on a speculative basis and are designed to accommodate a range of industrial uses, totaling approximately 947,000 square feet. The construction of the properties marks the commencement of the second phase of the park’s master-planned development. This milestone follows the recent disposition of one of the property’s buildings, which is fully leased to a global healthcare services and products company. The park’s other existing buildings are also fully occupied by Safavieh, KattSafe, Royal Interpack and Amazon. The general contractor on the project is Compass Commercial Construction, with design services provided by Curran Architecture and Kimley-Horn. The Indianapolis-based Colliers International team is managing leasing and marketing for the property. Ambrose has partnered with Fifth Third Bank on the construction loan. The post Ambrose Breaks Ground on Two Facilities at Indianapolis Logistics Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Ambrose breaks ground on 2 Phase 2 buildings at Indianapolis Logistics Park-NW: 947K SF speculative industrial.
Park in Whitestown, IN (Greater Indianapolis); existing buildings 100% leased (Amazon, Safavieh, healthcare anchor).
Construction loan via Fifth Third Bank; Colliers leasing; Phase 1 recently disposed to healthcare operator.
stories.summary: Ambrose broke ground on two speculative industrial buildings totaling approximately 947,000 square feet at Indianapolis Logistics Park – Northwest, a 104-acre modern industrial park in Whitestown, Indiana, marking Phase 2 of master-planned development. The park's existing buildings are fully leased to a diverse tenant base including Amazon, Safavieh, KattSafe, Royal Interpack, and a global healthcare services company. Fifth Third Bank provided the construction loan, with Colliers managing leasing and marketing.
stories.impact: Strong industrial demand and 100% occupancy in Greater Indianapolis logistics submarket validates speculative Phase 2 expansion. Indicates robust supply-chain and last-mile logistics activity near Indianapolis; healthcare tenant anchor signals diversification beyond e-commerce. While industrial, this reflects broader regional job/logistics growth that supports multifamily demand in Indianapolis metro—warehousing employment typically correlates with wage growth and workforce in-migration.

stories.title: BIG 4 Alliance Partners with Supply Chain Federation, CREDA SoCal
stories.excerpt: The BIG 4, an alliance between the cities of Commerce, Industry, Santa Fe Springs, and Vernon, announced on Monday a new partnership with the Supply Chain Federation, a national advocacy organization representing business and labor in goods movement, and CREDA SoCal to advance a regional approach to industrial development, workforce opportunity and supply-chain resilience across Southern California. As its first major initiative, the partnership will host the second annual BIG 4 Summit in 2027, bringing together regional and national stakeholders to advance conversations around industrial development, supply-chain resilience, workforce opportunity, economic competitiveness, industrial land, infrastructure and public-private collaboration. Since its formation in October 2025, the BIG 4 has established a unified voice for the shared interests and needs of its four cities and worked to expand business opportunities in the region through streamlined permitting, tax incentives, low-interest financing and reduced energy costs. In its first year, the BIG 4 has launched business incentives, convened the inaugural BIG 4 Summit, advocated for SB 1274 and closed its first joint economic development deal, keeping 80-year-old Juanita’s Foods and its manufacturing operations in Southern California. The post BIG 4 Alliance Partners with Supply Chain Federation, CREDA SoCal appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BIG 4 alliance (Commerce, Industry, Santa Fe Springs, Vernon, CA) partners with Supply Chain Federation & CREDA SoCal.
Initiative targets industrial development, workforce, supply-chain resilience; 2027 summit planned for regional stakeholders.
In first year (Oct 2025–2026), launched tax incentives, permitting streamlining, kept Juanita's Foods operations in SoCal.
stories.summary: The BIG 4 alliance—comprising the cities of Commerce, Industry, Santa Fe Springs, and Vernon in Southern California—announced a partnership with the Supply Chain Federation and CREDA SoCal to advance industrial development, workforce opportunity, and supply-chain resilience across the region. The partnership's first major initiative is hosting the second annual BIG 4 Summit in 2027, bringing together regional and national stakeholders. In its inaugural year, the BIG 4 launched business incentives, streamlined permitting, offered low-interest financing and reduced energy costs, and retained an 80-year-old food manufacturing operation.
stories.impact: Industrial-focused but signals SoCal's continued commitment to manufacturing/logistics base and workforce development. Retention of food manufacturing and focus on supply-chain jobs indicate regional strategy to compete for warehousing/industrial employment against inland metros. Multifamily developers in LA/Long Beach should monitor whether these incentives and workforce programs drive sustainable job growth and wage expansion in logistics and light industrial, both of which support rental demand in nearby residential corridors.

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Welcome Back, Speyer!
stories.excerpt: Back in 1997, one of the storied New York City real estate firms — Tishman Speyer — purchased one of the storied New York City properties: the Chrysler Building. Well, technically, what Tishman Speyer purchased was the skyscraper’s ground lease. The site was still owned by Cooper Union. Moreover, it was a ground lease that would get progressively more expensive in the coming years. (Shrewdly, Tishman Speyer sold a 90 percent interest in the building to the Abu Dhabi Investment Council in 2008 for $800 million.) When the property went up for sale again in 2019, expectations were significantly lowered about the value of the deal, given that the yearly payments to Cooper Union had by then ballooned from $7.8 million a year to $32.5 million. Still, market observers figured Chrysler was iconic, eye-catching, centrally located and beloved enough to fetch at least $500 million. After all, how many other properties of such status go on the market every day? But, when the ground rent was factored in, along with the fact that the property was in need of serious updates and repairs, the offers started coming in far, far lower than hoped for. The winning bid from RFR Realty was only $150 million. However, even that discounted price might have been too much. It wasn’t long before RFR and Cooper Union began butting heads about missed rent payments, necessary improvements and more. (RFR also had the poor luck of closing the deal in 2019, just before the office market was about to go into deep freeze.) RFR was eventually pushed out, and Cooper Union began looking around again for a savior. They apparently found one last week in the form of … Tishman Speyer? How much Tishman paid is still unknown, but the preliminary details indicate that the new land lease will last 150 years, and Tishman is putting up $235 million for improvements to the property. “We are pursuing an ambitious plan for the Chrysler Building at a historically strong moment for the Manhattan office market,” Rob Spey
bullets: Tishman Speyer purchased Chrysler Building ground lease in 1997; sold 90% stake to Abu Dhabi Investment Council for $800M in 2008.
Ground rent escalated from $7.8M/year (1997) to $32.5M/year by 2019; property requires significant capital repairs.
2019 sale expectations fell below $500M despite iconic status, location, and market presence due to ground lease burden and deferred capex.
stories.summary: Tishman Speyer purchased the Chrysler Building's ground lease (not fee) in 1997 from Cooper Union, which retained fee ownership. In 2008, Tishman Speyer sold a 90 percent interest to the Abu Dhabi Investment Council for $800 million. By 2019, when the property returned to market, annual ground rent had escalated from $7.8 million to $32.5 million, and the asset required substantial capital investment. Despite the building's iconic status, central location, and global recognition, market expectations for sale price fell significantly below the $500 million threshold, reflecting the burden of ground rent and deferred maintenance.
stories.impact: Illustrative of ground-lease risk in trophy Manhattan trophy properties and capital discipline in institutional real estate. While not multifamily, the dynamics—escalating ground rent, deferred capex reducing property value despite brand—parallel risks in long-term multifamily ground leases. Signals that even iconic assets trade at significant discounts when burdened by unfavorable lease economics; relevant to TCR's underwriting discipline on ground-lease assumptions and long-term escalation models.

stories.title: Charter School Inks 56K-SF Lease in Retail Center Near Miami Suburb
stories.excerpt: Charter school network BridgePrep Academy will open another location, this time inside a shopping center in Miami-Dade County. The school operator, which has 19 locations across Florida, signed a 56,000-square-foot lease at the open-air California Club Shopping Center in Ives Estates, near Aventura, 15 miles north of Downtown Miami. The 273,050-square-foot property, owned by RK Centers, sits west of Interstate 95 at 750 Ives Dairy Road. Other tenants at California Club include Planet Fitness, Five Below and Burlington. Waterways Preparatory Academy @ Kropp Annex, part of the public Dade County School District, previously leased BridgePrep’s new space up until at least last year. “Miami doesn’t have a surplus of properties that work for educational operators,” CBRE’s Scott Goldstein, who represented the tenant alongside Keith Edelman, said in a statement. “We moved quickly.” Some of the challenges include the lack of available properties that have the correct code and layout. Demand for grade schools, mostly for private ones, has skyrocketed in South Florida since the onset of the pandemic, when a slew of new-market companies opened offices and their employees moved in tow. To fix the issue, billionaire developer Stephen Ross is donating $100 million to Pine Crest School, a private school with locations in Fort Lauderdale and Boca Raton, to open another in West Palm Beach, Bloomberg reported. Another billionaire, Jeff Greene, has spent $50 million to build The Greene School, also in West Palm Beach, the Wall Street Journal reported. BridgePrep Academy and RK Centers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BridgePrep Academy signs 56K-SF lease at California Club Shopping Center, Ives Estates, Miami-Dade (15 miles N of downtown).
Charter school network with 19 FL locations; property also tenanted by Planet Fitness, Five Below, Burlington.
CBRE noted scarce supply of properties with correct code/layout for educational operators; post-pandemic demand for private schools surged.
stories.summary: Charter school network BridgePrep Academy signed a 56,000-square-foot lease at California Club Shopping Center in Ives Estates, Miami-Dade County, 15 miles north of Downtown Miami. The 273,050-square-foot open-air shopping center, owned by RK Centers and located west of I-95, also houses Planet Fitness, Five Below, and Burlington. CBRE brokers noted scarcity of properties with appropriate code and layout for educational operators, citing skyrocketing demand for private schools in South Florida since the pandemic.
stories.impact: Signals strong pandemic-driven migration and family formation in South Florida, evidenced by robust private school demand and willingness to commit 56K SF in retail centers. Reflects demographic shift toward family households in Miami-Dade; multifamily developers should track continued uptick in multi-bedroom unit demand and family-oriented amenities (schools, parks) in North Miami-Dade submarkets (Aventura, Sunny Isles, Bal Harbour periphery) as education-seeking households establish roots.

stories.title: Taco Bell’s Office Lease Largest in Orange County, Calif., in Five Years
stories.excerpt: Orange County, Calif.’s office market improved again in the third quarter thanks to a diverse set of corporate leases. Total vacancy improved to 15.4 percent, down from 17.1 percent a year ago, while average asking rents increased to $3.02 per square foot per month, up from $2.90 at the end of 2025, according to new data from JLL. Net absorption slipped slightly for the quarter, but remained positive on the year at 265,394 square feet, compared to negative 158,099 square feet for all of 2025. Tenants signed about 1.55 million square feet of leases during the quarter, led by Taco Bell’s 254,162-square-foot lease at Irvine Company’s Alton HQ, the largest office lease signed in Orange County in five years. (The maker of the Crunchwrap Supreme plans to relocate from its current Irvine headquarters in 2028.) Medical device maker Envista Holdings also signed for 101,800 square feet across three buildings, while an unnamed aerospace company took 173,057 square feet across two Airport Area properties, including 102,417 square feet at 4000 MacArthur Boulevard. The South County submarket posted the strongest quarterly absorption at 86,107 square feet, with Irvine Company’s Irvine Spectrum campus contributing 133,115 square feet. However, several other submarkets posted losses in absorption. Supply remains tight as Orange County has recorded no new office completions so far this year, and only one project — the 168,137-square-foot building underway at the Anaheim Ducks’ $5 billion mixed-use development — is under construction. The project is expected to deliver in the fourth quarter, and is already 23 percent pre-leased. Office conversions are also removing space from the market. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Taco Bell signs 254,162-SF office lease at Irvine Company's Alton HQ, Orange County—largest OC office lease in 5 years.
Orange County Q3 office vacancy fell to 15.4% (from 17.1% YoY); rents rose to $3.02/SF/month (from $2.90 end-2025).
YTD 2025 net absorption positive 265K SF (vs. negative 158K in all 2025); Taco Bell relocation from current HQ planned for 2028.
stories.summary: Taco Bell signed a 254,162-square-foot office lease at Irvine Company's Alton HQ in Irvine, California—the largest office lease in Orange County in five years. The company plans to relocate from its current headquarters in 2028. Orange County's office market improved in Q3 2025, with total vacancy declining to 15.4 percent from 17.1 percent year-over-year, while average asking rents increased to $3.02 per square foot per month from $2.90 at year-end 2025. Other Q3 leases included Envista Holdings (101,800 SF across three buildings) and an unnamed aerospace company (173,057 SF across two Airport Area properties).
stories.impact: Orange County office market stabilization (declining vacancy, rising rents, positive net absorption in 2025) suggests pent-up corporate demand releasing after years of pandemic-era challenges. However, limited direct multifamily relevance—office lease signings do not drive residential demand unless coupled with job creation or corporate relocation with headcount growth. TCR should monitor whether tech, aerospace, and consumer-facing tenant expansions in OC translate to wage growth and employment in-migration that supports multifamily demand; otherwise, office market recovery is independent signal.

stories.title: Yves Saint Laurent to Open Store at Kering’s 717 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Luxury French fashion house Yves Saint Laurent will open a new store at 717 Fifth Avenue, a new report revealed. According to a market report released by CBRE, the Kering-owned fashion house, once known as YSL for its founder, the late Yves Saint Laurent, will open in nearly 9,600 square feet in the base of the former Corning Glass Building that sits across East 56th Street from Trump Tower. Saint Laurent is currently at 3 East 57th Street, where it opened in 2003. That store was expanded to 14,071 square feet and renovated in 2015. According to property records, the original lease on East 57th Street ended in 2022 and had no renewal options. Since the fashion retailer is still there, the company likely signed a five-year extension during the pandemic, which would come due in October 2027. The building is managed by Buchbinder & Warren, which did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Kering bought the lower four floors at 717 Fifth Avenue in January 2024 for $963 million from Jeff Sutton’s Wharton Properties and SL Green Realty. The condominium has about 110,000 square feet that encompasses three floors of retail and one office floor. Most of the retail is occupied by Dolce & Gabbana and Armani. In December 2025, facing financial pressure, Kering sold a 60 percent stake to the large French private equity investment firm, Ardian, revaluing the commercial condominium to $900 million at $7,830 per square foot, but giving Kering a $690 million cash boost. It was expected at the time that Kering would begin to bring its own brands under its roof. Along with Saint Laurent, Kering encompasses Gucci, Balenciaga, Bottega Veneta, McQueen, Brioni plus Boucheron, Pomellato, DoDo, Qeelin, Ginori 1735 as well as Kering Eyewear. bullets: Yves Saint Laurent to open ~9,600-SF store at 717 Fifth Avenue (Kering-owned, Corning Glass Building base) across from Trump Tower.
Relocation from current 14,071-SF store at 3 East 57th Street (opened 2003, renovated 2015); original lease ended 2022 with no renewal.
Kering purchased lower 4 floors of 717 Fifth for $963M in Jan 2024 from Jeff Sutton's Wharton Properties & SL Green Realty.
stories.summary: Luxury fashion house Yves Saint Laurent will open a new store in approximately 9,600 square feet at 717 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, in the base of the former Corning Glass Building directly across East 56th Street from Trump Tower. The company is relocating from its current location at 3 East 57th Street, where it opened in 2003 and was expanded and renovated to 14,071 square feet in 2015. Kering, which owns the brand, purchased the lower four floors of 717 Fifth Avenue in January 2024 for $963 million from Wharton Properties and SL Green Realty.
stories.impact: Reflects luxury retail consolidation on Fifth Avenue (Midtown South) and Kering's portfolio optimization; does not directly impact multifamily supply, demand, or development economics. Fashion retail footprint changes signal consumer spending confidence in Manhattan but do not correlate to residential demand or pricing pressure relevant to TCR's multifamily development strategy.

stories.title: Northern Virginia Office Vacancy Falls Again as AI, Defense Demand Builds
stories.excerpt: Northern Virginia’s office market continued to tighten in the third quarter as more demand from artificial intelligence, technology and defense tenants bolstered weaker leasing activity. The market posted 672,378 square feet of positive net absorption during the quarter, reversing losses from the first half of the year tied to buildings being removed from the market, according to JLL. The National Science Foundation’s 380,000-square-foot move to 401 Dulany Street accounted for much of the gain. Northern Virginia’s office vacancy rate fell for a sixth straight quarter to 21.7 percent. Total available space dropped to 33.6 million square feet, its lowest level in a decade, and 25.5 percent below the 45.1 million-square-foot peak in 2023. Leasing activity slowed to just 1.3 million square feet on the quarter, with no deals of more than 100,000 square feet. AI, technology and defense companies committed to more than 300,000 square feet of net new space. And defense spending and tech investment are expected to continue driving momentum. Relocations and new leases have accounted for 58 percent of leasing so far in 2026 in a reverse to the renewal era of 2021 through 2023. Office supply is beginning to strengthen rents, according to JLL. Class A direct asking rents reached $42.51 per square foot per year, while overall direct asking rents averaged $38.13. JLL’s longer-term data shows asking rents have risen since 2022 for Trophy, Class A and Class B properties, while Class C rents have slipped. New construction remains virtually nonexistent, with only about 34,000 square feet underway. Meanwhile, more than 10 million square feet of existing office inventory has been proposed for redevelopment, a dynamic JLL expects will continue tightening the lower end of the market while limited Trophy supply pushes demand toward Class A properties. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Northern Virginia office vacancy fell to 21.7% (6 straight quarters of decline); available space dropped to 33.6M SF (lowest in decade, 25.5% below 2023 peak).
NSF's 380K-SF move to 401 Dulany Street drove much Q3 net absorption of 672K SF; AI, tech, defense tenants committed 300K+ SF of net new space.
Q3 leasing activity slowed to 1.3M SF; no large deals (100K+ SF); defense spending & tech investment expected to sustain momentum.
stories.summary: Northern Virginia's office market continued to tighten in Q3 2025, posting 672,378 square feet of positive net absorption, driven largely by the National Science Foundation's 380,000-square-foot move to 401 Dulany Street. Office vacancy fell to 21.7 percent for the sixth consecutive quarter, while total available space dropped to 33.6 million square feet—the lowest level in a decade and 25.5 percent below the 45.1 million-square-foot peak in 2023. AI, technology, and defense companies committed to more than 300,000 square feet of net new space, and both defense spending and tech investment are expected to continue driving momentum.
stories.impact: Northern Virginia office tightening signals strong tenant demand from federal, defense, and AI/tech sectors, historically concentrated in Tysons, Arlington, and Dulles Corridor submarkets. This employment growth—particularly NSF relocation and defense/tech expansion—will drive population and wage in-migration to NoVA, directly supporting multifamily demand in adjacent residential corridors (Arlington, Falls Church, Loudoun County submarkets). TCR should accelerate underwriting and acquisition in NoVA multifamily to capture rental demand from federal employee relocation, tech worker immigration, and sustained wage growth driven by defense spending and AI investment.
